**About Us**
------------

Lorikeet is redefining what customer support looks like — and we're just getting started.

We build AI that handles complex, high-volume support for fintechs, healthtechs, marketplaces, and delivery services. Not chatbot-tier AI. The kind that actually resolves tickets, gives support teams their time back, and raises the bar for what software can do.

We're backed by over $50M USD from QED, Blackbird, and Square Peg, with backing from operators like Claire Hughes Johnson (ex-Stripe COO) and Cristina Cordova (Linear COO), plus founders of Canva, Atlassian, and Airwallex. We're the first company since Canva to be funded at early stage by all three of Australia's top VC funds — which tells you something about the calibre of people who've looked closely at what we're building and said yes.

Our customers include some of the largest telehealth, fintech, and marketplace companies in the US and Australia — many handling over a million support tickets a year. The problems are real, the scale is real, and the work matters.

If you want to build something that genuinely changes how businesses and customers interact — this is the place.

**About the role**

Our Forward Deployed team works between our customers and our product. They take a customer’s whole support operation (the tickets, the systems, the policies) and turn it into AI agents that resolve real customer queries in production.

As an FDE intern, you’ll be part of that team from day one, not on a side project. The workflows you build will go live and handle real conversations for some of the largest fintech and healthtech companies in the US and Australia. You’ll have close support from the team and real ownership of the work you take on.

Day to day, you’ll:

* Dig into customers’ support tickets and data to find where AI can fully resolve queries, and where it can’t yet
* Build, test, and refine AI workflows from first draft through to production
* Help connect workflows to customer systems through APIs, and test integrations before they go live
* Join customer calls, share what you’ve found, and own defined parts of an implementation
* Use Claude Code and other AI tools to speed up analysis, build internal tooling, and improve how the team works

You’ll leave knowing how AI agents are deployed end to end at scale in regulated industries. You’ll also have hands-on skills in workflow design, API integrations, testing and evaluation, and LLM fundamentals, and experience turning a customer’s messy real-world problem into a working solution.

**We’d love to talk if you**

* Are curious and learn fast. You pick up new tools quickly and enjoy figuring things out.
* Are technically confident. You don’t need to be a software engineer, but you’re comfortable reading API docs and working with data.
* Sweat the details. You notice when something’s off, ask good questions, and follow through.
* Communicate clearly with technical and non-technical people alike.
* Are genuinely interested in AI. It’s a bonus if you’ve experimented with LLMs or built something with AI tools on your own.

**What's unique about this opportunity?**
-----------------------------------------

**A culture that's genuinely different.** Low ego, high trust, no tolerance for talented jerks. We work efficiently, keep hours flexible, and actually mean it — because life outside work matters. We're committed to building a diverse team and actively encourage applicants from underrepresented backgrounds. We care far more about user obsession and eagerness to learn than traditional credentials.

**A front-row seat to building something meaningful.** We're Series A and moving fast. You'll have real scope to shape the product and the company — not just execute someone else's vision.

**Performance recognized in real time, not on a calendar.** Promotions happen when you're ready — leadership meets every six weeks specifically to identify and recognize strong performers, so you're never waiting for an arbitrary review window to move up.

**We're AI-native, and we'll make you AI-native too.** Every person at Lorikeet uses AI in their day-to-day work (current favourite: Claude Code), with unrestricted access and no usage limits. You'll leave with skills that matter for the next decade of work.

**Twice a year, the whole company flies to Hawaii.** Headquartered in Sydney, with teams spanning the US and UK — which means getting everyone in the same place is something we invest in seriously. We spend the time hacking on ideas, building things together that wouldn't otherwise exist, and making memories that remind you why you joined a startup in the first place.

**A recruitment process built on respect, not hoops.** We keep it simple: a couple of informal chats to share our story and hear yours, followed by a paid ~two-day work trial. The work trial is genuinely the best part — you'll work on real problems alongside the actual team, get a true feel for how we operate, and we'll both come out of it knowing whether this is the right fit. No trick questions, no take-homes that disappear into a void. Just real work, done together.

If you're from an underrepresented background and don't tick every box, please reach out anyway. We know firsthand that diverse teams perform better, and we're proud that our team reflects a broad spectrum of identities and lived experiences.

***Use your molecular biology skills to help detect cancer earlier through liquid biopsy research***

A single tube of blood can carry traces of a tumour long before conventional tests find it. Liquid biopsy is reshaping how cancer is detected, monitored and treated, and the quality of that science rests on meticulous sample handling and reliable laboratory data. As a Research Assistant in the cancer research team at Macquarie Medical School, you will help generate exactly that.

Working within the Faculty of Medicine, Health and Human Sciences, you will process and analyse human biological samples, contribute to the investigation of circulating tumour-derived biomarkers and molecular features of cancer, and help build the datasets that underpin publications and future clinical translation. Structured training will be provided in liquid biopsy methodologies and related molecular biology techniques, so you can extend your technical repertoire while contributing from day one.

This is a valuable opportunity for an early-career researcher with a foundation in molecular biology who enjoys precise bench work and wants to grow within a research-intensive environment. You will work closely with the lead researcher and wider cancer research team, with access to modern laboratory facilities, professional development programs and a research community spanning biomedical, translational and health services domains.

**About the Role**

Reporting to the Deputy Dean, Research and Innovation and working under appropriate supervision, you will provide technical and research assistance across the cancer research program. Your responsibilities will include:

  

* Performing routine laboratory procedures and molecular biology techniques in line with established protocols and standard operating procedures
* Receiving, processing, aliquoting and storing biological samples, including blood-derived specimens, with close attention to sample integrity and traceability
* Undertaking training in liquid biopsy methodologies and contributing to the analysis of circulating tumour-derived biomarkers and other molecular analytes
* Assisting with nucleic acid extraction, quality assessment and preparation of samples for downstream molecular analyses, including sequencing applications
* Recording, organising and maintaining experimental and sample data in laboratory records, databases and electronic systems, with appropriate version control
* Assisting with quality control, preliminary data processing, targeted literature searches and the preparation of datasets, figures, tables, reports and manuscripts
* Identifying and reporting protocol deviations, technical issues or unexpected results, and maintaining laboratory areas, equipment and reagents in line with research governance, ethics, biosafety and WHS requirements

Please note that work hours may vary from time to time to accommodate operational needs.

**Lead the digital experience that puts students at the heart of education.**

  

Champion innovation across the student journey, bringing together people, technology and insight to create seamless, engaging and inclusive digital experiences that enable students to connect, learn, thrive and succeed.

Every student at Macquarie University interacts with our digital services from the moment they apply, through enrolment, learning and all the way to graduation. This newly established role owns the digital experience approach for our student and education domain, supported by a dedicated team, and the development capability focused solely on the student experience.

As the Student and Education Digital Experience Lead, you are the primary IT partner, the IT "front door" for the Student Services domain. You will work alongside Student Shared Services, Deputy Deans, Faculty Executive Directors, the Dean of Students Office and the PVC Education to connect academic and service priorities with technology capability, so that student needs, service performance, investment decisions and delivery roadmaps stay aligned with the University's strategic objectives.

This newly established role is central to Macquarie’s customer-focused, experience-led IT operating model, aligned with IT’s 2027 Workforce Plan and the shift toward domain-focused delivery leadership. It is a high-impact, highly visible position at the intersection of higher education, student services and technology, with the scope, resources and accountability to shape digital experiences for our students.

**About the Role**

Reporting to the Chief Information and Digital Officer, you will guide the student and education digital experience end to end. Your focus will include:

  

* Developing and maintaining the Student Experience roadmap, domain backlog and prioritisation approach, aligned to business priorities, service outcomes and strategic objectives.
* Coordinating demand through a single domain view, so work is prioritised and routed appropriately across experience teams, platform teams, project delivery pathways and operational improvement activity.
* Guiding your team and dedicated development capability to deliver a prioritised backlog of improvements, with attention to backlog health, sequencing, dependencies, delivery predictability and value realisation.
* Translating student insights, service performance information and journey pain points into prioritised initiatives with measurable outcomes.
* Partnering with Platform Owners, Architects, and the Cyber, Service Management, Data and AI functions so student experiences make best use of enterprise platforms, reusable capabilities and architectural standards, with security considered from the earliest stages of planning and design.
* Progressing the responsible adoption of AI-enabled capabilities across the domain, with appropriate governance and oversight.
* Using customer, service, operational and business data to establish meaningful performance measures, generate actionable insights and monitor digital adoption, product performance and benefits.
* Reporting domain performance, delivery confidence, adoption, risks, benefits and priorities through Quarterly Business Reviews and other governance forums.
* Guiding the transition from project-based delivery to enduring product and experience-team ownership, including capability uplift across product, Agile, DevSecOps, analytics, design and change practices.

**About us**

Macquarie University Information Technology (MQ IT) embraces the university mission to be bold, distinctive, progressive, and transformational. Information Technology is a trusted business partner with an ethos of service, and we pride ourselves in the application of a strong collaborative partnership approach to transformation across the University. We strive for the efficient provision of services to better support the areas where we should be unique across the education, research, and health portfolios within the University.

**About You**

You are an experienced digital, product or service leader with a strong understanding of the higher education sector, university environments and the student experience, with an appreciation of academic and education contexts. You are confident engaging in technical conversations and skilled at building effective relationships across various stakeholders, academic colleagues, platform teams and multidisciplinary teams.

* Strong leadership, facilitation and communication skills, including guiding multidisciplinary teams, enabling organisational change, building capability, and conveying complex information clearly to executive stakeholders and governance forums.

We don’t do hair. But we do straighten out some of the world’s biggest challenges.

We’re engineers, scientists, designers, architects, planners, advisors, innovators and change makers, committed to making energy, water and communities sustainable for generations to come.

Since 1928, we’ve been wholly owned by our employees. Today, we are 11,000 diverse and skilled individuals working in over 160 offices across five continents — Asia, Australia, Europe, North and South America, and the Pacific region.

  

**Who could you be at GHD?**

Our Location Intelligence team utilises Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and a range of spatial and non-spatial data to enable our clients to understand relationships between data, undertake analytics and visualisations, and transform data into actionable insights. This team of specialists are looking for Graduate Spatial Analysts to join them as part of our 2027 Graduate Program.

We’re looking for someone who:

* has recently graduated (or is a current student expecting to graduate by the end of 2026) with a degree and/or major in areas such as Spatial/Geospatial Science, Surveying, Geographical Information Systems (GIS), Earth Science, Cartography, Geography or similar. Alternatively, you could be studying towards a degree in Engineering or Computer Science, with a passion for GIS.
* Has an interest in working in consulting and the engineering and environment sectors
* has good verbal and written communication skills.
* is enthusiastic and willing to learn across a wide range of projects.

We have positions are available in several of our GHD offices, commencing in February 2027:

* Melbourne
* Adelaide
* Canberra
* Sydney (Piccadilly)
* Brisbane or Toowoomba
* Hobart

Our two-year Graduate Development Program is designed to give you a smooth start to your consulting career. Alongside your peers, managers and mentors, we’ll help you detangle any challenges along the way.

  

**A frizz-free application process:**

We want your journey to be as smooth as possible, so here’s everything you need to help you prep like a pro:

* **Your CV:** This gives us a snapshot of what you’ve studied and your experiences, both paid and unpaid.
* **A cover letter:** Think of this as your chance to show us where you’d love to grow within GHD, while letting your communication skills shine.
* **Your transcript:** This helps us understand what you’ve been learning, from your core subjects to the electives that sparked your curiosity.
  

**Your journey to joining GHD:**

Here’s what to expect, step by step:

* **Screening:** We review applications as they come in, but be mindful that the bulk of our screening happens after applications close, so don’t worry if you don’t hear from us right away.
* **Virtual Assessments:** If you make it through the first stage, you’ll record some answers to a few straightforward questions and complete some cognitive games. This helps us get a better sense of your work style and alignment to GHD Graduate roles.
* **Meet the team:** If you’re successful, you’ll have a face-to-face interview (wherever possible) with your prospective team. We’ll chat through some *behavioural based questions* to learn more about your skills and experience. It’s also a chance for you to get to know us!
* **Offer:** Congratulations! We’ll talk through all the finer details, like salary, your start date, our onboarding process and what to expect before your first day.

We’re committed to being as inclusive as possible and giving everyone an equitable chance of getting through our application process. **If you identify as someone who is neurodiverse or have a disability** and need adjustments to any part of the process, let us know in your application form—we’re here to help.

  

**Start dates and opportunities**

Most of our full-time roles kick off in February 2027, though there may be the possibility of earlier start dates for some teams. Plus, there might also be casual work opportunities throughout your final year of study to give you a head start.

  

**Ready to shine?**

If you’ve got your documents polished and prepped, the application should only take 10-15 minutes. Apply now and take the first step toward an exciting career in consulting.

  

**GHD: The Power of Commitment**

At GHD, we don’t just believe in the power of commitment, we live and breathe it every day.
  
  
Community impact is important to us, influencing how we work, our projects and how we give back.
